subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron output target contract, and if so which file, channel, session, fallback, and status semantics belong in core?
rationale: The requested behavior is useful but changes public cron configuration, scheduler-owned file writes, cross-channel delivery, and invisible session state; automation should not choose those boundaries without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor a core output contract
options.body: Define a single core cron output API with explicit security rules, status reporting, migrations/docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to existing delivery fixes
options.body: Keep this issue open as an umbrella but repair concrete existing delivery regressions in narrower bug reports such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/56078.

options.title: Decline new core routing
options.body: Leave cron output routing to current `delivery`, message-tool, webhook, and plugin patterns and close or redirect the broader API request later.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a core output contract
recommendation.body: Define a single core cron output API with explicit security rules, status reporting, migrations/docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The initial cron delivery-mode owner is the best available routing candidate for deciding whether this public cron API should expand.
